newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl, Chirac reaffirm EMU criteria, timetable.
newsitem.headline: Kohl, Chirac reaffirm EMU criteria, timetable.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and French President Jacques Chirac reaffirmed their commitment to the entry criteria and timetable for Europe's single currency at a meeting here on Wednesday evening, Bonn said on Thursday.

Government spokesman Peter Hausmann said the leaders also expressed their determination to achieve a positive outcome at June's European Union summit in Amsterdam, which will wrap up institutional reforms to cope with planned EU enlargement.
Hausmann said in a statement that "the common reaffirmation of criteria and timetable for economic and monetary union" was one of the main themes of the meeting.
Kohl and Chirac met for an informal dinner at the Bonn chancellery and the pair will hold further meetings before the June summit.
Bonn, hit by high unemployment and slack tax revenues, is struggling to live up to its commitment to a strict reading of European monetary union's (EMU) governing Maastricht treaty.

Most independent economists say the budget deficit will this year overshoot the target of three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) set by Maastricht for countries to qualify for the planned start of EMU in 1999.
